Monitoring the hydrogen mining platform was basically weeks of deep space boredom punctuated by moments of sheer terror. When an alarm sounded, you sometimes had only minutes to react to avoid catastrophe. You learned pretty quickly that you had to suspend operations if you left the station for any length of time.

When my routine was unexpectedly interrupted by a distress beacon, I was intrigued. I couldn't imagine why anyone would be out this far.

The gas giant the station orbited was far from any established trade routes and normally the only ship I saw was the supply ship that showed up every 3 months or so. I reluctantly took the processors offline, knowing full well I was going to blow my quota.

I climbed into the cramped service pod and did my pre-trip. Everything was nominal so I released the docking clamps and fired her up. I had decided to name the pod Gracie. It's the little things that keep you sane out here. I locked on to the beacon and set Gracie on auto, then settled in for a nap.

She woke me as we approached the ship. It seemed to be a derelict. Well this was curious. Why would an old wreck like this be sending out a distress call?

I suited up since the ship didn't appear to have a docking station and went EVA. The cockpit was dark, the pilot's chair empty. The only sign that any systems were even functional was a switch on the instrument panel blinking green.

I had nothing to lose, so I hit the switch. The cockpit was filled with a voice that I will never forget. Soft, melodious and definitely feminine. The voice just kept repeating the word "Welcome" over and over again. None of this made any sense to me.

As I reached the open hatch I realized with a start that something was terribly wrong.

Gracie was gone.

I should have mentioned it earlier, but Gracie was one of the old first generation A.I. pods. She could be quite temperamental at times. I trusted her with my life, but we have worked together a very long time now.

I remember the first time I needed her help. One of the primary energy buffers had gone on the fritz and we had to go out and repair it.

Gracie had decided it was not a convenient time to repair the buffer and instead decided we would go on a sightseeing tour of the planet below. I know service pods aren't really intended for orbital flights, but she knew every trick in the book. She orbited the planet like a pro, I could tell this wasn't her first time. To be honest, I think she enjoyed showing off.

I begged and pleaded with her for hours to take us back so we could complete our mission. She was having none of it.

I finally got an idea. I explained how much I would miss her when they removed me from my post because I had failed my mission. That did the trick. She must have grown fond of me over the course of our flight together and finally gave in.

Gracie wasn't going to put up with anyone taking her away from me. I made myself comfortable and took another nap. Whoever took her was in for one wild ride, I knew it was just a matter of time.

I eventually woke up and looked out the hatch. There was my Gracie. Her canopy was wide open and the pilot seat empty.

I examined her carefully. Someone had tried prying off the access hatch to set her to manual control only.

Gracie would never stand for that.
